text: DeFi isn't one thing — it's five categories of protocol, built on top of each other. Know these five, and you can place almost any new protocol you encounter without learning it from scratch.

DEXs and AMMs swap tokens by formula instead of an order book — Uniswap and Curve. Lending protocols like Aave and Compound let you supply for interest or borrow against collateral. Derivatives like GMX and dYdX trade price exposure without holding the asset. Stablecoins hold steady value — USDC fiat-backed, DAI crypto-collateralized. Yield aggregators like Yearn automate moving capital between all of these.

Watch one dollar move: swap USDC for ETH on an AMM, supply that ETH as collateral on a lending protocol, borrow a stablecoin against it, then deploy that stablecoin into a yield vault depositing into an AMM pool. Four categories, one sequence, no bank anywhere in it.

Every category solves one of two problems: how strangers trade without an order book, solved by AMM math, and how strangers lend without a credit check, solved by collateral instead of trust. That's exactly why this course spends two full chapters on AMMs and lending.
Five categories, two load-bearing primitives. Next up: composability — how these categories actually stack together.
